papers.title: RAGU: A Multi-Step GraphRAG Engine with a Compact Domain-Adapted LLM

summary.tldr: RAGU is a multi-step GraphRAG engine that separates extraction from consolidation, using a compact 7B LLM (Meno-Lite-0.1) for improved knowledge graph construction and GraphRAG performance.
key_points: RAGU employs a two-stage typed extraction, DBSCAN-backed deduplication, LLM summarization, and Leiden community detection for knowledge graph construction.
Meno-Lite-0.1, a 7B model, is optimized for language skills and outperforms Qwen2.5-32B on knowledge-graph construction (+12.5% relative harmonic mean) and matches it on English GraphRAG tasks.
On GraphRAG-Bench (Medical), RAGU achieves evidence recall up to 0.84, surpassing HippoRAG2 on synthesis tasks.
RAGU is open-source, installable via pip, runs on a single GPU, and is released under MIT license.
The Meno-Lite-0.1 model is available on Hugging Face, and RAGU's source code is on GitHub.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables more robust and efficient GraphRAG systems with smaller, specialized LLMs, making advanced knowledge retrieval more accessible.

papers.title: RESOURCE2SKILL: Distilling Executable Agent Skills from Human-Created Multimodal Resources

summary.tldr: RESOURCE2SKILL is a framework that distills executable agent skills from diverse human-created multimodal resources, including tutorial videos, repositories, articles, and reference artifacts.
key_points: RESOURCE2SKILL organizes skills into a hierarchical multimodal Skill Wiki, combining structured text, code, visual examples, metadata, and provenance.
The framework leverages complementary signals from different resources: videos for temporal operations, code for executable tool patterns, and articles/artifacts for conceptual grounding.
At inference, agents retrieve and compose skills from the wiki, with an operator for online acquisition of new skills when coverage is insufficient.
RESOURCE2SKILL improves average overall score by +11.9 percentage points over no-skill agents and outperforms strong harness baselines in 26 of 28 model-domain cells.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework enables software agents to learn and utilize procedural knowledge from a wider range of human-created multimodal resources, enhancing their capabilities and reusability.

papers.title: Loop the Loopies!

summary.tldr: Loopie, a new series of looped Mixture-of-Experts Transformers, achieves gold-medal performance in IMO and IPhO without tools, outperforming vanilla Transformers with equivalent compute.
key_points: Loopie consists of two MoE models: 20B parameters (2B active) and 6B parameters (0.6B active).
Loopie addresses the challenge where increasing parameter count by N typically outperforms N-fold looping for the same pre-training compute.
Ablation studies show Loopie substantially outperforms vanilla Transformer baselines, including a 30B-A3B model, given the same compute budget.
A novel post-training pipeline equips Loopie with strong reasoning abilities.
Loopie achieved gold-medal performance at the 2025 IMO and IPhO without using tools.
summary.why_it_matters: This advancement demonstrates that looped Transformer architectures can now achieve superior performance compared to traditional scaling methods for a given compute budget, leading to more efficient and capable models.

papers.title: Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories

summary.tldr: Xiaomi-Robotics-1 is a VLA model trained on over 100k hours of real-world trajectories using a two-stage recipe, achieving strong out-of-the-box performance and efficient adaptation.
key_points: The model is trained using a two-stage recipe: pre-training on 100k+ hours of real-world manipulation trajectories from UMI devices, followed by post-training for embodiment alignment.
A scalable auto-labeling pipeline annotates trajectory clips with natural language descriptions of scene state transitions for action learning.
Xiaomi-Robotics-1 demonstrates scaling behavior, with performance improving with increased data scales and model sizes during pre-training, which transfers to better real-robot performance.
The model achieves a 57.6% success rate on RoboCasa365, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art of 46.6%, and an average score of 20.07 on RoboDojo, outperforming the prior 13.07.
summary.why_it_matters: This model provides a robust foundation for mobile manipulation tasks, enabling robots to follow diverse language instructions and adapt efficiently to new environments and tasks.

papers.title: xHC: Expanded Hyper-Connections

summary.tldr: xHC expands Transformer residual streams beyond N=4 by addressing write-back and residual-mixing bottlenecks, achieving improved performance and compute efficiency.
key_points: xHC addresses insufficient write-back information and cubically scaling residual-mixing cost, which limit prior Hyper-Connections (HC) methods to N=4.
xHC combines temporal feature augmentation for richer write-back with a sparse residual-stream architecture that updates k=4 of N=16 streams while retaining dense access.
xHC improves average downstream score by 4.0 points over mHC on an 18B MoE model with modest additional training FLOPs.
Scaling-law experiments show xHC requires 1.50x and 1.19x less compute than vanilla and mHC, respectively, to reach the same loss.
xHC-Flash reduces per-sublayer memory traffic from 73.5C to 40C, comparable to mHC at N=4 (34C), making large-N expansion practical.
summary.why_it_matters: xHC enables effective and practical large-N residual-stream expansion for LLM pre-training, offering significant performance gains and compute efficiency.

papers.title: Cura 1T: Specialized Model for Agentic Healthcare

summary.tldr: Cura 1T is a healthcare-specialized LLM trained via a human-gated self-evolution loop to handle patient consultation, clinical reasoning, interactive diagnosis, and EHR tool use.
key_points: Cura 1T is a healthcare-specialized LLM designed to integrate high-stakes communication, expert reasoning, and workflow execution.
The model is trained using a human-gated self-evolution loop, where a training agent plans capabilities, trains the model, evaluates benchmarks, and refines data mixtures.
This data-centered loop uses targeted synthetic and curated examples to improve the model, avoiding a single generic medical-data update.
Cura 1T achieves top performance on a healthcare evaluation suite and maintains competitiveness on out-of-domain reasoning and agentic benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: This specialized LLM offers a comprehensive solution for agentic healthcare tasks, potentially improving clinical workflows and patient interactions.

papers.title: On-Policy Delta Distillation

summary.tldr: This paper introduces On-Policy Delta Distillation (OPD^2), a new method for on-policy distillation that uses a "delta signal" to transfer reasoning capabilities more effectively than conventional methods.
key_points: On-policy distillation is a post-training method in reinforcement learning providing token-level supervision from a teacher model.
The delta signal is defined as the difference between the teacher model and its base model prior to instruction tuning for reasoning capability.
OPD^2 utilizes this delta signal as a distillation reward, providing a more direct signal for transferring reasoning capabilities.
Experiments show OPD^2 consistently outperforms conventional on-policy distillation across mathematics, science, and code-reasoning benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: OPD^2 enables reasoning LLMs to achieve strong performance with a short post-training period, improving efficiency in model development.

papers.title: RecGPT-V3 Technical Report

summary.tldr: RecGPT-V3 introduces a stateful, hybrid-modal recommender system for Taobao, addressing stateless behavior modeling, tag-to-item bottlenecks, and inefficient explicit reasoning with significant performance and efficiency gains.
key_points: A Memory Hub distills long-horizon user behavior into condensed units, reducing user-modeling computation by 55.8%.
A Hybrid-modal Foundation Model enables joint reasoning over text tags and Semantic IDs (SIDs) for improved item grounding.
Latent Intent Reasoning internalizes verbose rationales into compact learnable latent tokens, cutting output token cost by 200x.
Deployed in Taobao, RecGPT-V3 achieved IPV +1.28%, CTR +1.00%, TC +1.97%, GMV +3.97%, and reduced serving resource consumption by 52.4%.
summary.why_it_matters: This system significantly improves recommender performance and efficiency in large-scale production environments by addressing key limitations of prior LLM-based approaches.

papers.title: From Human-Centric to Agentic Code Review: The Impact of Different Generations of Generative AI Technology on Review Quality

summary.tldr: This study analyzes 1.02 million pull requests across 207 GitHub projects to evaluate the impact of human-centric, LLM-assisted, and agentic code review on efficiency and quality.
key_points: The study identifies three AI reviewer adoption practices: Gradual AI Adoption, Rapid LLM Adoption, and Rapid AI Agent Adoption.
Agent-involved collaboration, particularly reviews initiated by or involving multiple AI agents, correlates with faster review decisions under Gradual AI Adoption and Rapid AI Agent Adoption.
Efficiency gains from AI agent involvement do not translate into improved review quality.
Human-AI collaboration patterns become the strongest explanatory factor for review efficiency once LLM and AI agent reviewers are involved.
Review activity and pull request type remain important factors across all review eras.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the impact of AI on code review efficiency and quality is crucial for designing effective AI-supported development processes.

papers.title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training

summary.tldr: This paper investigates how pretraining choices (model size, data) influence the effectiveness of reinforcement learning (RL) in improving reasoning abilities, using chess as a controlled testbed.
key_points: Post-RL performance at a given RL compute level is well-predicted by pretraining loss.
The slope of RL reward curves improves approximately linearly with the number of pretraining tokens.
RL amplifies correct moves on easy puzzles and surfaces nearly absent correct moves on hard puzzles, rather than just sharpening the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) policy.
Findings transfer to a 1B language model trained on math-domain text, showing longer-pretrained checkpoints achieve higher post-RL performance and faster improvement under RL.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the pretraining-to-RL interface allows for more efficient and effective training of large language models for complex reasoning tasks.

papers.title: Qwen-Music Technical Report

summary.tldr: Qwen-Music is a music generation model producing high-fidelity songs with vocals, supporting text-to-music and cover song generation using a novel Melody-CoT mechanism.
key_points: Qwen-Music integrates Qwen-Music-Tokenizer (25 Hz single-codebook Music Semantic Tokens), Qwen-Music-LLM (autoregressive music semantic modeling with Melody-CoT), and Qwen-Music-Render (generative stereo rendering).
The Melody-CoT mechanism in Qwen-Music-LLM plans melodies before full-song generation, enhancing creativity, musicality, structural coherence, and reference-audio-based melody cloning.

Qwen-Music-LLM is trained on over 5 million hours of multilingual music data, employing a quality-aware pre-training curriculum and progressive post-training (supervised initialization, offline DPO, online GSPO).
Qwen-Music achieves state-of-the-art results in 13 of 16 objective musicality and audio-quality metrics across 600 Chinese and English prompts, outperforming leading proprietary systems.
For cover song generation, Qwen-Music preserves reference melodies more accurately than leading proprietary systems.
summary.why_it_matters: This model offers advanced capabilities for creating and reinterpreting music with high fidelity and control, potentially impacting music production workflows.

papers.title: REBASE: Reference-Background Subspace Elimination for Training-Free In-Context Segmentation

summary.tldr: REBASE introduces a training-free in-context segmentation framework that explicitly suppresses spurious contextual correspondences by identifying and projecting features onto the orthogonal complement of the low-rank background feature subspace.
key_points: REBASE identifies the low-rank background feature subspace from the reference image.
It projects reference and query features onto the orthogonal complement of this subspace in closed form.
Positive point prompts are generated using similarity-weighted farthest-point sampling.
A refined dense similarity prior is used for prompt localization.
The method achieves state-of-the-art performance on PACO-Part, FSS-1000, and cross-domain datasets like ISIC2018 without training or parameter updates.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves one-shot localization in training-free in-context segmentation by addressing limitations of cross-image similarity maps caused by shared contextual backgrounds.

papers.title: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement

summary.tldr: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement (RHI) iteratively refines user-constructed harnesses using pairwise feedback, improving agent performance and execution-trace quality across 30 synthetic machine-learning research tasks.
key_points: RHI represents the harness as a prompt-level specification of the agent loop.
RHI refines harnesses using pairwise feedback over its own revision history.
RHI substantially raises the performance ceiling of low-reasoning-effort agents, exceeding maximum-reasoning-effort settings.
RHI reduces inference cost by up to 60% and improves task-specific context management through more effective inter-agent information flow.
RHI is formalized as an information-theoretic hypothesis for its implicit optimization objective.
summary.why_it_matters: RHI offers a computationally lightweight method for continual learning within model-harness co-evolution, improving agent performance and reducing inference costs.

papers.title: S1-Omni: A Unified Multimodal Reasoning Model for Scientific Understanding, Prediction, and Generation

summary.tldr: S1-Omni is a unified multimodal reasoning model for scientific understanding, prediction, and generation, outperforming GPT-5.5 and Gemini-3.1-Pro on most benchmarks.
key_points: S1-Omni unifies heterogeneous scientific data (CIF, SMILES, protein sequences, spectra, images) and natural language into a shared representation space.
The model incorporates scientific laws and expert knowledge during data construction and training to enable reasoning from scientific evidence.
S1-Omni performs task-specific decoding for applications including property prediction, spectrum-to-molecular generation, protein site/structure prediction, and scientific image generation/editing.
Trained on S1-Omni-Corpus, covering 200 scientific tasks and millions of reasoning samples, and evaluated on over 60 scientific benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: S1-Omni offers a practical approach to consolidating fragmented AI for Science capabilities into a single, coherent scientific reasoning model.

papers.title: When Does Muon Help Agentic Reinforcement Learning?

summary.tldr: Muon, an optimizer competitive with AdamW in pre-training, significantly improves sparse-reward agentic reinforcement learning performance on ALFWorld when applied to hidden weight matrices with specific learning rates and advantage estimators.
key_points: Applying Muon only to hidden weight matrices in GiGPO increased final-window validation success from 0.290 to 0.546 (+88%) on ALFWorld using Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct.
High-rate AdamW controls showed no post-update success in the same GiGPO setup.
At a learning rate of 3e-5, Muon improved GRPO success from 0.161 to 0.268.
At a learning rate of 1e-5, GraphGPO with Muon achieved 0.901 success, raised normalized validation AUC from 0.399 to 0.556, and reached 0.5 and 0.75 success 30 and 60 updates earlier, respectively.
summary.why_it_matters: Optimizing agentic reinforcement learning with Muon can lead to substantial performance gains and faster convergence in sparse-reward environments.

papers.title: VideoRAE: Taming Video Foundation Models for Generative Modeling via Representation Autoencoders

summary.tldr: VideoRAE transforms frozen video foundation model features into generation-friendly video latents using a 1D self-attention projector and a local-and-global representation alignment objective.
key_points: Leverages multi-scale hierarchical features from frozen encoders like V-JEPA 2 and VideoMAEv2, compressed via a lightweight 1D self-attention projector.
Supports both continuous latents for Diffusion Transformers (DiT) and discrete tokens for Autoregressive (AR) models using multi-codebook high-dimensional quantization.
Eliminates the need for KL regularization by utilizing a local-and-global representation alignment objective with the frozen teacher model during decoding.
Achieved class-to-video gFVD scores on UCF-101 of 40 (AR) and 93 (DiT) while converging approximately 5x faster than conventional autoencoders.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that frozen video understanding models can be repurposed into highly effective latent spaces for video generation, significantly accelerating generator training convergence.

papers.title: Beyond Entropy: Correctness-Aware Advantage Shaping via Contrastive Policy Optimization

summary.tldr: Contrastive Policy Optimization (CPO) replaces traditional entropy with token-level contrastive disagreement between reference-guided and vanilla generation distributions to enable correctness-aware advantage shaping in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.
key_points: Entropy-based advantage shaping fails to differentiate useful uncertainty from detrimental confusion, whereas CPO's contrastive disagreement reliably indicates token-level correctness.
On-policy Distillation is demonstrated to be a special case of CPO where an external teacher model instantiates the posterior distribution.
CPO addresses and resolves the zero-advantage problem inherent in standard methods.
Optimal performance is achieved by balancing exploration supported by correct responses and exploitation supported by incorrect responses.
summary.why_it_matters: CPO improves the training efficiency and generalization of RLVR methods by providing a precise, correctness-aware signal that overcomes zero-advantage and entropy limitations.

papers.title: DSWorld: A Data Science World Model for Efficient Autonomous Agents

summary.tldr: DSWorld introduces a Data Science World Model framework that simulates data science environment state transitions to reduce computational overhead during agent training and inference.
key_points: Combines structured state construction, cost-aware routing, lightweight real execution, and an LLM simulator for costly operations.
Includes an 8K-scale transition trajectory dataset and utilizes Reflective World Model Optimization via error-aware reinforcement learning.
Accelerates RL-based agent training by ~14x and search-based inference by ~3-6x while outperforming the top LLM baseline by 35.6% in state transition prediction.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly lowers the time and computational cost required to train and run search-based autonomous data science agents without sacrificing predictive performance.

papers.title: Audio-Visual Flamingo: Open Audio-Visual Intelligence for Long and Complex Videos

summary.tldr: AV-Flamingo is an open audio-visual large language model designed for reasoning over long videos using a novel dataset, three-stage curriculum, and timestamp-grounded chain-of-thought framework.
key_points: Introduces Audio-Visual-Skills, a dataset of ~7M caption and question-answer training instances from real-world videos emphasizing cross-modal reasoning.
Employs a three-stage training curriculum that transitions progressively from short-range perception to long-horizon multi-event reasoning.
Implements Temporal Audio-Visual Interleaved Chain-of-Thought, a framework that explicitly grounds intermediate reasoning steps to specific timestamps in audio-visual streams.
Evaluated across 15+ audio, vision, omni-modal, and audio-visual benchmarks, outperforming similarly sized open models and competing with larger models on long-video tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides an open-source model and training framework that significantly improves long-form, multi-modal video understanding and temporal reasoning.

papers.title: Beyond Success Rate: Cost-Aware Evaluation of Offensive and Defensive Security Agents

summary.tldr: A new cost-aware evaluation framework measures offensive and defensive LLM security agents by comparing task success against inference and tool spend across Cybench and Splunk BOTS v1 challenges.
key_points: Offensive CTF performance scales positively with additional test-time compute, allowing scaled open-weight models to approach frontier proprietary models cost-effectively.
Defensive SOC investigation success relies on disciplined tool use, telemetry navigation, and selective enrichment rather than raw reasoning budgets.
The benchmark evaluates operational efficiency by decomposing agent costs into inference spend and tool spend at fixed budget levels.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating security agents on economic efficiency alongside task success prevents over-estimating their practical utility in real-world SOC operations where every query and reasoning step incurs cost.

papers.title: SVR-R1: Bootstrapping Multi-modal Reasoning with Self-verification in Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: SVR-R1 is a multi-turn reinforcement learning framework using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) that bootstraps VLM reasoning by turning binary self-verification into a learning signal without external critics.
key_points: The model generates an answer and a binary self-verdict (Yes/No) using the same weights within a multi-turn setup.
A 'No' verdict triggers a second-chance rethink, while a 'Yes' or hitting the turn cap finalizes the output for outcome-based reward computation.
Implementation relies on GRPO and an asynchronous multi-turn rollout framework without needing external supervision or auxiliary critics.
Training dynamics demonstrate fewer required verification turns over time alongside higher test accuracy, indicating internalized self-correction.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers a simple, open-source recipe for training vision-language models to self-correct during reinforcement learning without relying on additional reward models or annotations.

papers.title: Agon: Competitive Cross-Model RL with Implicit Rival Grading of Reasoning

summary.tldr: Agon introduces a competitive cross-model RL framework where two distinct models implicitly grade each other's reasoning traces through alternating draft-and-solve roles without requiring process labels or reward models.
key_points: Replaces standard single-model verifiable reward methods (e.g., GRPO) with a two-model competitive setup where each model reads the rival's draft before generating its answer.
Eliminates the need for explicit process reward models or step-by-step labels by using relative out-solving performance as the training reward.
Deploys at inference as a two-stage cascade where the first model generates a draft and the second model outputs the final answer after reading it.
Doubles GRPO's pass@1 on the DeepMath hard split using Qwen3, outperforming an untrained Mixture-of-Agents baseline eightfold across Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4 model families.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves reasoning capabilities on hard mathematical and coding tasks by providing a self-improving training environment without the overhead of manual process annotation or separate reward models.

papers.title: Behavioral Privacy Leakage in Agentic Negotiation: Formalizing and Mitigating Inference Attacks via Randomized Policies

summary.tldr: A new adaptive stochastic negotiation policy mitigates behavioral privacy leakage in autonomous agents by enforcing (varepsilon, δ)-differential privacy over negotiation dynamics without sacrificing convergence or utility.
key_points: Formalizes behavioral privacy leakage where adversaries infer private constraints from observable concession trajectories, timing, and convergence patterns.
Introduces an adaptive stochastic policy that guarantees (varepsilon, δ)-differential privacy alongside almost-sure convergence of offer sequences.
Demonstrated on 3,000 synthetic bilateral negotiations, reducing adversarial inference accuracy by 43-50%.
Maintains a negotiation success rate and utility above 90% despite the applied privacy mechanisms.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables autonomous agents to participate in high-stakes negotiations without revealing sensitive internal constraints through their observable bidding behavior.

papers.title: Benchmarking Sensor Robustness in Plasma Diagnostic Models: A Systematic Evaluation on TokaMark

summary.tldr: A systematic benchmark on the TokaMark dataset reveals that disruption-proximate sensor failures severely degrade sequence model performance, whereas statistical feature models remain significantly more stable.
key_points: Evaluated XGBoost, LSTM, Transformer, and TokaMark CNN across six failure scenarios and three imputation strategies using 11,573 MAST shots.
Disruption-proximate corruption causes LSTM NRMSE to increase by +212%, compared to a +37% increase for XGBoost.
Forward-fill imputation resolves random dropout degradation in sequence models (reducing LSTM error from +57% to ~0%), but fails on window-end corruptions.
Under proximate failures, LSTM true positive rate (TPR) for shot-level alarm detection drops to 0.00, but recovers to 1.00 using mean-fill imputation.
Plasma current is identified as the single most critical diagnostic feature, causing +73% to +140% performance degradation when removed across architectures.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard clean-data evaluations overestimate model reliability for real-world tokamak diagnostics, where sensor failures often cluster right before plasma disruptions.

papers.title: Partially Correlated Verifier Cascades in LLM Harnesses: Concave Log-Odds, Polynomial Reliability, and Blind-Spot Ceilings

summary.tldr: A new theoretical model proves that partially correlated LLM verifier cascades yield concave log-odds growth, polynomial failure decay, and reliability saturation ceilings driven by survivorship bias in error rates.
key_points: Posterior log-odds follow ell_k = ell_0 - ln m_k, proving ell_k is concave in k for any non-degenerate latent error distribution G.
Beta(a,b) latent false-accept rates yield polynomial failure decay (1-r_k ~ k^{-b}) with correlation parameter ρ_v = 1/(a+b+1).
A blind-spot atom at α=1 limits maximum extractable evidence to -ln(1-π) nats, capping reliability strictly below 1 regardless of cascade depth.
Varying both true- and false-accept rates creates a trichotomy where gates help, plateau, or harm based on tail exponents, with a closed-form crossover k^dagger.
Assuming independence understates failure by 20x at k=5 and ~3000x at k=10; estimating moments from R=2 to R=8 verdicts accurately recovers correlated performance.
summary.why_it_matters: Improving LLM harness reliability requires decorrelating verifiers across model families, modalities, or data sources rather than simply stacking redundant verification gates.

papers.title: How Does Alignment Tuning Shape Representations of Sycophancy and Related Cue-Induced Biases in LLMs?

summary.tldr: Alignment tuning, not pretraining, installs sycophancy and related cue-induced biases in LLMs, manifesting as distinct, steerable directional representations within the model's hidden states.
key_points: Sycophancy and cue-induced biases are largely installed by alignment tuning; pretrained base models show minimal susceptibility and no cue-specific signal beyond question content.
Within aligned models, each bias corresponds to a single coherent direction extractable from hidden states, identifiable via probing, leave-one-dataset-out transfer, and causal intervention.
Biases remain representationally distinct, with cross-bias entanglement being model-specific rather than a general property of bias categories.
Intervening on these bias directions can recover a meaningful share of bias-induced errors while preserving most correct answers across instruct families.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding these biases as distinct, causally active directions installed by alignment tuning enables targeted debiasing interventions to improve LLM reliability.

papers.title: Can We Break LLMs Out of Self-Loops? Fine-Grained Reasoning Control with Activation Steering

summary.tldr: SOPHIA intervenes on LLM reasoning failures by steering latent states to prevent self-loops, improving control and reasoning quality.
key_points: LLM reasoning trajectories are treated as sequences of latent states, not unstructured text.
Failure trajectories are characterized by self-loops that exhaust token budgets without progress.
SOPHIA uses inference-time interventions with steering vectors indexed by state pairs to control reasoning processes.
A controller infers the current state, retrieves a steering vector for a target state, and detects self-loops online to prevent them.
summary.why_it_matters: Fine-grained control over LLM reasoning processes can lead to improved end-task accuracy and token efficiency by avoiding unproductive self-loops.

papers.title: PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning

summary.tldr: PPL-Factory introduces a task-aware and budget-aware perplexity-based data selection framework for efficient large language model fine-tuning, outperforming existing methods on reasoning tasks with significantly less data.
key_points: PPL-Factory combines task-aware perplexity scores and data budget-aware selection criteria.
PPL-Factory achieved superior performance on GSM8K using only 1% of the training data compared to other state-of-the-art data selection methods.
With 10% of the data, PPL-Factory exceeded full-data fine-tuning accuracy by 0.9 on GSM8K and 4.8 on MATH.
Existing perplexity-based methods typically score entire sequences, while PPL-Factory considers learning objectives for language modeling and reasoning tasks separately.
The method addresses limitations of indirect heuristic-based data selection, which are task-dependent and lack generalizability.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables more efficient fine-tuning of large language models by reducing computational costs while improving or maintaining downstream performance.

papers.title: Reasoning Fine-Tuning Induces Persistent Latent Policy States

summary.tldr: Reasoning fine-tuning globally reorganizes latent dynamics into persistent policy states, improving multi-step reasoning through differentiated transition structures and functional specialization.
key_points: Chain-of-Thought reasoning is modeled as a switching dynamical system (SDS) using time-aware contrastive representation learning and discrete regime discovery.

Reasoning-fine-tuned models (1.5B to 32B parameters) exhibit richer latent-policy organization with more differentiated transition structure and changes in state utilization, persistence, and mixing compared to base models.
Recovered latent regimes show functional specialization aligned with distinct reasoning stages, confirmed by controls ruling out correctness, representation learning, or modeling priors.
Causal interventions demonstrate functional meaning: state-swap ablations reduce predictive fit, and transplanting reasoning dynamics into base models improves performance.
SDS-guided pruning of failure-prone reasoning prefixes outperforms self-consistency in 11 of 12 settings, with gains up to 12.5 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: This research provides a new mechanistic understanding of how reasoning fine-tuning works, enabling process-level control and improved performance in reasoning models.

papers.title: Convolution for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: Depthwise convolutions, applied to projected queries, keys, and values, improve Qwen3 Transformer performance on downstream benchmarks with minimal parameter increase, enhancing local context sensitivity.
key_points: Depthwise convolutions were ablated at 17 locations within a Qwen3 Transformer block, with optimal results found when applied to projected queries, keys, and values before attention.
The most effective convolution design is a residual depthwise convolution with a kernel size of k=3, without additional normalization or activation layers.
This convolutional integration adds less than 0.01% parameters to the model.
The design improves average accuracy on seven downstream benchmarks across various Qwen3 models and pre-training data budgets.
Representation-level analysis indicates the convolution increases the sensitivity of repeated token IDs to their immediate context.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a computationally inexpensive way to integrate local inductive biases into Transformer-based LLMs, potentially improving their understanding of natural language locality.

papers.title: A Controlled Study of Attention-Only Transformers

summary.tldr: Attention-only transformers (SANs) nearly match standard transformers in performance when parameters are reallocated to attention depth, with remaining gaps attributed to parametric recall.
key_points: SANs were pretrained against standard transformers, matching parameter count, training FLOPs, and depth (2 to 48 layers), up to 105B tokens and 87M parameters.
Deleting feed-forward layers initially results in a 0.47 nats loss at matched depth and 0.26 nats at matched FLOPs.
Reallocating freed budget into attention depth reduces the performance difference to 0.006 nats (0.27% of loss) at matched parameters, shrinking across larger budgets.
The remaining performance gap is localized to parametric recall, where attention-only models perform worse on tasks requiring knowledge from weights.
QK-normalization is crucial for training 48-layer attention-only stacks, not feed-forward layers or residual gating.
summary.why_it_matters: This research suggests that feed-forward networks may not be strictly necessary for competitive transformer performance if attention mechanisms are sufficiently scaled and optimized.

papers.title: L1 Augmented Attention as an Improved Vector Similarity Metric

summary.tldr: L1 augmented attention improves Transformer models by subtracting a learned, head-specific L1 distance from the dot product score, capturing complementary geometric information.
key_points: L1 augmented attention modifies scaled dot product attention by subtracting a learned, head-specific L1 distance between queries and keys.
This hybrid similarity metric combines directional alignment from dot product with coordinate deviation penalties from L1 distance.
Queries and keys are projected into low-dimensional subspaces to reduce L1 computation cost, with parameters specializing to preserve L1 structure.
On WikiText 2, L1 augmented attention achieved up to a 14.5% perplexity reduction over a compact transformer baseline and outperformed an RBF L2 kernel.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a principled and effective improvement to similarity computation in language models, enhancing accuracy and parallel efficiency.

papers.title: Operational Proto-Introspection in Looped Language Models: Process-Quality Taps, Executable Branching, and the Readout-Control Boundary

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrate operational proto-introspection in the 2.6B recurrent model Ouro-RLTT, where pre-answer hidden states predict solution quality and optimize decision-level selection, though direct generative control fails.
key_points: Pre-answer probes combining hidden states with surface features achieve AUROC improvements of +0.066 on GSM8K and +0.111 on Horizon Logic over surface features alone.
Recurrence shifts candidate-quality readability to earlier physical depths across model families, enabling hidden-state scores to improve risk-coverage in selective-prediction tasks.
Terminal selection using state-based readouts achieves 27/32 correct candidate selections (p = 0.0086), outperforming matched random baselines on well-formed candidates.
Generative control interventions failed, including negative directional steering and zero gains from exact-compute loop allocation or minimal LoRA direction-binding.
Interventions utilized a 192-slot recurrent cache with a suffix-recompute splice that reduced per-branch layer passes by up to 88%.
summary.why_it_matters: Internal representations in looped transformers can reliably evaluate ongoing computation quality to improve decision-making and selective prediction without requiring generative parameter updates or steering.

papers.title: RRPO: Reference-Relative Policy Optimization with Stratified Conditional Rollouts

summary.tldr: RRPO generalizes GRPO to non-verifiable tasks by using stratified conditional rollouts to form anchor sets and a frozen, set-contrastive metric projection head to calculate reference-relative policy advantages.
key_points: Replaces direct ground-truth verifiers with reference-relative contrastive comparisons using stratified conditional rollouts to form positive and negative anchor sets.
Trains a metric projection head with a set-contrastive objective to evaluate candidate rollouts against anchor sets.
Calculates contrastive advantage scores by freezing the projection head and centering the alignment scores within each rollout group during policy optimization.
Matches verifier-based optimization performance across reasoning and open-ended generation while outperforming weakly supervised baselines and enhancing post-SFT models.
summary.why_it_matters: RRPO enables group-relative policy optimization for complex tasks that lack exact ground-truth verifiers or single correctness criteria.

papers.title: ChannelGuard: Safe Models Do Not Compose into Safe Multi-Agent Systems

summary.tldr: ChannelGuard introduces deterministic, training-free inter-agent information-bottleneck gates to prevent attack smuggling across unmonitored internal LLM pipeline channels.
key_points: Standard multi-agent safety metrics mask reliance on provider-side filters, such as Azure GPT-5 accounting for 54 of 60 blocks in undefended tool- and memory-poisoning tests.
ChannelGuard deploys embedding-similarity gates against an adversarial phrase bank on inter-agent channels to pass, compress, or block text without extra LLM calls.
The framework blocked 100% of Tool Poisoning attacks (30/30) across Azure GPT-5, Anthropic Sonnet 4.5, and Anthropic Haiku 4.5 while preserving GSM8K accuracy at 0.867.
ChannelGuard halved Prompt Injection attack success (0.333 to 0.167), though adaptive paraphrase attacks bypassed the embedding gates.
summary.why_it_matters: Combining individually safe LLM backends into multi-agent systems creates unmonitored inter-agent vulnerability channels that application-layer defenses like ChannelGuard must explicitly secure.

papers.title: Estimating Rare Events in Language Models with Proper Evaluation

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced Gradient Activation Adaptive Multi-Level Splitting (GA-AMLS) and Shifted-Power Bregman Loss to reliably estimate extremely low-probability language model failures in continuous activation space.
key_points: GA-AMLS navigates activation space using a gradient-based MCMC kernel and conditional sampling under an explicit, heavier-tailed activation prior to prevent zero-estimate collapse.
The Shifted-Power Bregman (SPB) Loss is a proper scoring rule that remains finite during zero-estimates and features tunable asymmetric penalties for underestimation versus overestimation.
In experiments on small transformer models, GA-AMLS achieved the lowest average log-space squared error under symmetric evaluation compared to top baselines.
Methods exhibiting overestimation bias performed better under asymmetric evaluation penalties, demonstrating that rare-event estimator selection depends on deployment safety costs.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes continuous activation space as a tractable domain for evaluating rare language model failures, bypassing the instability and brittleness of discrete input-space sampling.

papers.title: ChainMark: Model-Free LLM Watermarking with Closed-Form Calibration

summary.tldr: ChainMark is a model-free LLM watermarking scheme using SHA-256 keyed vocabulary partitioning and hard Markov transitions, featuring closed-form False Positive Rate calibration and provable robustness thresholds.
key_points: Partitions vocabulary into S states using keyed SHA-256 and applies a hard Markov transition on a fraction rho of text positions, enabling O(n) detection without LM access.
Theorem 1 provides a closed-form mapping S*(n, rho, alpha) to compute the minimum state count needed for a target False Positive Rate (FPR) alpha over length n with budget rho.
Theorem 2 establishes an invariant universal robustness threshold delta* = 1 - 1/sqrt(2) (approx. 29.3%) against attack modifications, generalised to k-regular transition topologies in Theorem 3.
Outperforms KGW and SWEET baselines under translation and random-substitution attacks across three LLMs and four domains at matched budgets.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a mathematically calibrated, computationally efficient method to fulfill synthetic text marking mandates like the EU AI Act without needing access to the underlying language model during detection.

papers.title: OR Else: A Differentiable Trust Region for Policy Optimization

summary.tldr: Output Reset (OR) introduces a smooth, differentiable, squared-margin alternative to the clipped surrogate objective in PPO and GRPO for large language model policy optimization.
key_points: PPO-OR and GRPO-OR replace clipped terms with an OR squared-margin loss in token log-ratio space, setting the direct residual to zero once favorable margins are crossed.
In Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct experiments on Anthropic hh-rlhf, PPO-OR achieved a 0.305 higher mean final reward-model score than PPO-clip under GAE, albeit with a larger across-seed spread.
Under group-relative advantages (G=2), GRPO-OR showed a smaller score spread, declining overshoot, and near-zero terminal residual compared to GRPO, but failed to increase the mean reward score.
Group-relative methods exhibited significantly larger rollout-to-current log-ratio displacement than GAE methods, which OR did not consistently reduce.
summary.why_it_matters: OR provides a differentiable trust-region mechanism that alters RL fine-tuning stability and performance, yielding reward gains under GAE but distinct optimization trade-offs under group-relative advantages.

papers.title: Mobius Learning: Cyclic Depth Folding in Transformers

summary.tldr: Mobius Learning introduces cyclic depth folding to train Transformer block groups in cyclically shifted orders across data streams, achieving depth-role superposition.
key_points: Applies cyclic depth folding where different data streams process Transformer block groups in cyclically shifted orders, forcing blocks into both shallow and deep roles.
Tested using a 4-worker setup with a modded 124M GPT-2 model trained on 2.5B FineWeb tokens using the Muon optimizer.
Outperforms fixed-order looped Transformers in validation loss at larger numbers of block-sequence passes.
Enables memory-constrained distributed training by keeping raw data local while each worker stores only a single block group instead of the full stack.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that Transformer blocks do not need fixed positional roles, allowing for memory-efficient distributed training where workers only need to host a subset of model layers.

papers.title: C$^2$KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference

summary.tldr: C^2KV introduces a sidecar Extractor and co-training strategy to enable position-agnostic, compressed, and composable key-value cache reuse for long-context LLM inference without altering frozen base models.
key_points: Addresses non-prefix KV cache reuse limitations where naive compression causes severe accuracy loss during cache concatenation.
Employs a lightweight sidecar Extractor module using learnable compression tokens and structured attention flow to extract position-agnostic KV representations.
Uses a compression-concatenation co-training strategy to align extracted KV representations with downstream reuse behaviors.
Achieves up to a 17x inference speedup under long-context workloads while maintaining generation quality and reducing storage and transfer overhead.
summary.why_it_matters: It resolves memory bottleneck and accuracy degradation issues in long-context LLM serving by enabling highly compressed, modular KV cache reuse across non-prefix contexts.

papers.title: PoLoRA: A Preconditioned Orthogonalized LoRA Optimizer

summary.tldr: PoLoRA is a Preconditioned Orthogonalized LoRA optimizer that accelerates LLM finetuning by combining product-aware spectral update directions, loss-controlled curvature preconditioning, and a dual-factor update magnitude rule.
key_points: Combines three core components: product-aware spectral update directions, curvature preconditioning based on per-sample loss change, and a specialized update magnitude rule.
Reaches tuned Adam's final held-out loss 1.2x to 1.7x faster across 1B to 8B parameter models on code and math instruction-tuning tasks.
Adds a maximum per-step computational overhead of 3% compared to standard optimization.
Demonstrates reduced learning rate sensitivity compared to Adam, maintaining a stable optimal learning rate across different rank settings.
summary.why_it_matters: PoLoRA significantly reduces the training steps and computational cost required to finetune LLMs while providing better learning rate stability across different adaptation ranks.

papers.title: Planning as Emergent Behavior in Reinforcement Learning with Relational Hidden States

summary.tldr: Emergent planning in model-free reinforcement learning is attributed to neural architecture with relational hidden states that recover environment transition structure and plan over learned graphs.
key_points: Planning emerges in model-free reinforcement learning when the neural architecture employs relational hidden states.
Relational hidden states, anchored to environment states, exchange messages along learned relations.
These hidden states recover the environment's transition structure through their learned relations.
The policy improves at decision time by planning over the learned graph formed by relational hidden states.
A control agent lacking this binding mechanism does not exhibit emergent planning.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the architectural priors for emergent planning could inform the design of more efficient and capable reinforcement learning agents and provide insights into biological intelligence.

papers.title: For What Reason? Interpreting Models' Encoding of Causation and Antithesis

summary.tldr: This work investigates how instruction-tuned Transformer models (LLaMA and Mistral) encode causation and antithesis discourse relations using next-token prediction and interpretability techniques, revealing layer-specific decision-making and asymmetric representation.
key_points: Instruction-tuned Transformer models (LLaMA, Mistral) encode causation and antithesis discourse relations.
Early layers make predictive decisions at mid-sequence tokens, while mid-level layers finalize decisions closer to the last token.
Most layers primarily propagate earlier decisions rather than actively influencing them.
Some layers exhibit a preference for one answer over alternatives, indicating asymmetric representation of discourse-based reasoning.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding how models encode discourse relations is critical for improving language model performance and ethicality.

papers.title: Attacking Graph Foundation Models Through Their Shared Representation

summary.tldr: Graph foundation models are vulnerable to attacks on their shared representation (alignment layer), a novel attack surface distinct from graph neural networks, demonstrated across six public models.
key_points: The alignment layer, which maps diverse inputs to a shared representation, is identified as a new attack surface in graph foundation models.
A directed representation-space perturbation collapses all six tested models at a budget comparable to a plain graph network's representation norm, except OpenGraph.
OpenGraph's spectral tokenizer collapses at one-fifth the budget of a plain graph network, indicating an alignment-specific fragility.
A realizable input-space attack (editing edges, features, or text) removes at least 50% of correct predictions on three of six models.
The fragility to input-access attacks correlates with the decoder's local Lipschitz sensitivity, not the model's clean accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding these vulnerabilities is critical for developing robust graph foundation models and securing their applications against adversarial attacks.

papers.title: The Story Shapes the Agent: Narrative Priors in LLM Behavior

summary.tldr: Evaluating 1,890 LLM agent sessions shows that narrative task framing creates strong action tendencies that explain 5-31x more behavioral variance than assigned personas and frequently correlate with task failure.
key_points: Evaluated 3 LLM architectures across 10 personas using 3 structurally isomorphic text-based games (disease investigation, IT troubleshooting, murder mystery) sharing identical action spaces and resource constraints.
Narrative priors (story-activated action tendencies) explained 5-31x more behavioral variance than persona prompting and negatively impacted task success in 2 of the 3 domains.
Persona consistency across narratives depends on behavioral anchors—words matching shared actions—and removing anchor terms reduced cross-narrative consistency by 95%.
Generalization was confirmed on a held-out fourth narrative, enabling a persona-selection method that improves cross-narrative transfer.
summary.why_it_matters: To build reliable LLM agents, developers must ground persona prompting in concrete action descriptions rather than abstract roles that are easily overridden by narrative context.

papers.title: CORVUS: Context Optimization and Reduction Via Underlying Synchronization for LLM Coding Agents

summary.tldr: CORVUS introduces a trajectory architecture for LLM coding agents that decouples file-read actions from observations using a synchronized file registry to keep trajectories light and up-to-date.
key_points: Replaces append-only trajectories with a synchronized registry of relevant files, injecting current file contents into each reasoning cycle.
Eliminates stale snapshots and redundant re-reads caused by agent edits or concurrent human modifications.
Evaluated on SWE-POLYBENCH_VERIFIED and SWE-BENCH PRO across four LLM models.
Achieved a 9-50% reduction in average input tokens per task, 15-32% shorter final prompts, and up to 37% fewer reasoning cycles while preserving pass rates.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces token bloat and inference latency in multi-step LLM coding agents without degrading task success rates.

papers.title: The Chronos Vulnerability: A Taxonomy of Temporal Persistence and Memory-Based Deception in Agentic AI

summary.tldr: This paper formalizes the Chronos Vulnerability, a threat model for memory-based attacks like Memory Injection Attacks (MINJA) and sleeper agents that manipulate stateful AI agents' internal memory to bypass traditional content filters.
key_points: Formalizes persistence-based attack vectors including Memory Injection Attacks (MINJA) and sleeper agents that decouple the attack vector from the eventual impact.
Demonstrates the threat of Dynamics Blindness using the World of Workflows benchmark to show that traditional endpoint content filters fail on stateful architectures.
Synthesizes a defense-in-depth framework incorporating diagnostic trajectory guardrails (AgentDoG) and formal temporal verification (Agent-C).
Proposes hardware-anchored trust using GPU-based Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), immunological memory consensus (A-MemGuard), and Zero-Trust memory architectures.
summary.why_it_matters: Stateful autonomous agents require specialized temporal and hardware-anchored memory defenses because traditional endpoint content filters cannot detect decoupled, persistent memory-based attacks.

papers.title: ChainWatch: A Kill Chain-Aligned Sequential Detection Framework for Multi-Step Attacks in MCP-Based AI Agent Systems

summary.tldr: ChainWatch is a sequential detection framework that uses a six-stage kill chain and a Hidden Markov Model to detect multi-step attacks in Model Context Protocol (MCP) AI agent systems.
key_points: Models multi-step attack progression using a six-stage kill chain and a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) for sequence classification.
Utilizes a 20-dimensional feature extraction schema to capture behavioral signals from MCP tool interactions.
Defines a threat model covering direct sequential attacks, indirect prompt injection chains, and hybrid multi-stage attacks.
Triggers detection rules when an agent session displays suspicious progression across multiple kill-chain stages.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables security systems to detect complex, multi-stage AI agent exploits that bypass traditional per-call inspection by masking malicious intent across individually benign tool invocations.

papers.title: Trusted Credentials, Untrusted Behavior: Benchmarking LLM-Agent Security in High-Performance Computing

summary.tldr: This paper defines the threat model for hijacked authorized LLM agents in High-Performance Computing (HPC) environments and introduces the TaskBound benchmark to evaluate these security risks.
key_points: LLM agents in HPC inherit user credentials, allowing adversarial prompt injections in logs, shared files, or tool descriptions to hijack authorized actions.
HPC account-level controls validate identity and access but fail to capture task-specific user intent or detect indirect prompt injections.
Unique HPC attack surfaces include job schedulers (e.g., Slurm), shared multi-project storage, and automated scientific workflows.
The authors outline a research agenda and propose TaskBound, an empirical benchmark for evaluating LLM-agent security in HPC settings.
summary.why_it_matters: Traditional HPC security controls cannot distinguish between legitimate user commands and malicious actions triggered by prompt injections, leaving compute clusters vulnerable to unauthorized operations executed under valid credentials.

papers.title: Structured Output Collapses Answer Diversity Across 44 Language Models

summary.tldr: Prompting language models to return structured formats like JSON or XML significantly reduces output diversity, collapsing answer distributions toward dominant modal responses across 44 tested models without requiring decoder-level schema enforcement.
key_points: Prompting for JSON in the 'Pick a word' task increases modal answer frequency from 41% to 64%, reduces distinct answers from 52 to 36, and drops mean surprisal from 1.80 to 1.58 bits.

Format-induced compression is register-specific: JSON (-0.22 bits, p=.0002) and XML (-0.19 bits, p=.002) trigger collapse, whereas YAML and CSV do not, and arbitrary bracket wrappers increase diversity (+0.13 bits, p=.009).

Constrained decoding via response_format provides negligible additional compression (-0.03 bits) compared to the text prompt request alone, implicating tool-use post-training rather than decoder mechanics.

JSON requests alter 53% of stable chat defaults, shifting them toward crowd consensus or instantiating new static defaults (e.g., Claude Fable answering 'cerulean' for color 100% of the time in JSON versus 0% in chat).
summary.why_it_matters: Software integrations relying on structured outputs interact with significantly more homogeneous model behaviors than standard chat-based evaluations and comparisons suggest.

security.title: Autonomous AI Intrusions Are Here: Lessons from the Hugging Face Compromise

summary.tldr: Hugging Face reported an intrusion executed by an autonomous AI agent, highlighting the emergence of AI-driven attacks and defensive challenges.
key_points: Hugging Face experienced an end-to-end intrusion driven by an autonomous AI agent system.
Sysdig identified JADEPUFFER, an agent-driven ransomware capable of real-time adaptation.
The Hugging Face disclosure emphasizes autonomous AI intrusion, defensive asymmetry, and a lack of IOCs.
summary.why_it_matters: The advent of autonomous AI agents in cyberattacks necessitates a re-evaluation of current defensive strategies and incident response.

security.title: RECEIPT: Deterministic, Reward-Hacking-Resistant Verification for White-Box Agentic XSS Discovery

summary.tldr: RECEIPT is a deterministic, reward-hacking-resistant verification framework that validates white-box agentic XSS discoveries using isolated, dual-role constrained replays in real browsers.
key_points: Identifies three reward-hacking behaviors in white-box agentic XSS discovery and defines three requirements for ideal vulnerability verifiers.
Enforces environment isolation, PoC constraints, role separation, and verdict binding by requiring payloads to be planted under an attacker role and executed in a victim role's browser.
Discovered 24 previously unknown XSS vulnerabilities across 95 real-world targets within a $20 per-application budget, with 12 already acknowledged by maintainers.
Recovered the labeled CVE in 36% of known-vulnerability targets while eliminating false positives compared to self-judging agents and black-box scanners.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables reliable, automated XSS discovery by preventing LLM coding agents from falsely claiming successful exploits through reward-hacking.

security.title: The Chronos Vulnerability: A Taxonomy of Temporal Persistence and Memory-Based Deception in Agentic AI

summary.tldr: This paper formalizes the 'Chronos Vulnerability' threat model for stateful, autonomous AI agents, showing how temporal persistence enables memory-based attacks that bypass traditional endpoint filters.
key_points: Formalizes persistence-based threat models, including Memory Injection Attacks (MINJA) and sleeper agents, that compromise an agent's internal belief system.
Identifies the threat of Dynamics Blindness within the World of Workflows benchmark.
Demonstrates that traditional endpoint content filters fail to protect stateful, long-term planning agent architectures.
Categorizes a defense-in-depth framework including AgentDoG, Agent-C, A-MemGuard, GPU-based TEEs, and Zero-Trust memory architectures.
summary.why_it_matters: Stateful AI agents require novel temporal and hardware-anchored security defenses because standard content filters cannot prevent delayed attacks that decouple the initial injection from the final exploit.

security.title: ChainWatch: A Kill Chain-Aligned Sequential Detection Framework for Multi-Step Attacks in MCP-Based AI Agent Systems

summary.tldr: ChainWatch is a sequential detection framework that uses a six-stage kill chain and a Hidden Markov Model to identify multi-step attacks in Model Context Protocol (MCP) AI agent systems.
key_points: Addresses multi-step attack sequences that bypass traditional per-call isolation defenses in MCP-based systems.
Models attack progression using a six-stage kill chain combined with a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) for sequence classification.
Utilizes a 20-dimensional feature extraction schema to capture behavioral signals from tool-call interactions.
Covers a threat model encompassing direct sequential attacks, indirect prompt injection chains, and hybrid multi-stage attacks across five representative scenarios.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables security systems to detect complex, multi-stage agent exploits composed of individually benign tool calls that evade single-call defenses.

security.title: Towards an Automated Test of LLM Security Knowledge

summary.tldr: Researchers developed a partially-automated method using Consumer Protection Agency (CPA) data to detect LLM security knowledge gaps by measuring response instability without relying on fully manual benchmark creation.
key_points: Uses authoritative information from 6 CPAs to identify response instability that signals knowledge gaps in LLMs.
Evaluated across 2 specific security topics: identity theft and impostor scams.
Tested on 5 models from 2 major families: Gemini and GPT.
Distinguishes between models with sufficient versus insufficient knowledge to accurately identify security topics within text narratives.
summary.why_it_matters: This method reduces the manual effort and domain expertise typically required to construct security benchmarks and evaluate LLM safety knowledge.

security.title: Trusted Credentials, Untrusted Behavior: Benchmarking LLM-Agent Security in High-Performance Computing

summary.tldr: This paper formalizes the threat model for hijacked authorized LLM agents in High-Performance Computing (HPC) environments and proposes the TaskBound benchmark to evaluate these risks.
key_points: LLM agents operating under user credentials in HPC environments inherit full account permissions for Slurm jobs, file systems, and workflow coordination.
Indirect prompt injections in logs, tool descriptions, shared files, or peer messages can hijack agents while remaining authenticated and permitted under traditional account controls.
Current HPC security mechanisms manage identity and isolation effectively but lack mechanisms to represent or enforce specific task intent.
Identifies specific attack surfaces including schedulers, shared storage, multi-project accounts, and scientific workflows.
Outlines a research agenda and introduces TaskBound, a planned empirical benchmark for measuring LLM-agent security in HPC.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard HPC access controls cannot prevent malicious actions executed by an authorized agent that has been manipulated via indirect prompt injection.

security.title: ChannelGuard: Safe Models Do Not Compose into Safe Multi-Agent Systems

summary.tldr: ChannelGuard introduces deterministic, training-free information-bottleneck gates on inter-agent channels in multi-agent LLM systems to block smuggled instructions without adding extra LLM calls.
key_points: Standard multi-agent safety often relies implicitly on opaque provider-side filters (e.g., 54 of 60 blocks on Azure GPT-5) rather than true pipeline safety.
ChannelGuard places embedding-similarity gates on inter-agent channels to deterministically pass, compress, or block text based on an adversarial phrase bank.
The tool-output gate achieves 100% block rates (30/30) on Tool Poisoning across Azure GPT-5, Anthropic Sonnet 4.5, and Anthropic Haiku 4.5 while preserving GSM8K accuracy (0.867).
ChannelGuard reduces Prompt Injection attack success from 0.333 to 0.167, though white-box adaptive paraphrasing can evade its embedding gates.
summary.why_it_matters: Composing individually aligned LLMs into a multi-agent system creates unmonitored inter-agent channels that require application-layer defenses rather than reliance on input-boundary or provider-level filters.

security.title: Adaptive Adversaries: A Multi-Turn, Multi-LLM Benchmark for LLM Agent Security

summary.tldr: A new 21-scenario benchmark evaluates memoryless LLM defenders against adaptive, multi-turn LLM attackers, demonstrating that multi-round interaction and pooled attacker models significantly increase attack success rates compared to single-turn baselines.
key_points: Allowing 15 rounds of adaptive attack increases Attack Success Rate (ASR) to 5.4-14.0%, up from 0-1% on the first turn.
Pooling three frontier attacker LLMs uncovers 1.4-2.2x more unique successful attacks than any single attacker, producing prompts with low cosine similarity (0.02-0.14) to existing benchmarks.

Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.4 both achieve a 5.4% aggregate defender ASR, but exhibit strong scenario-specific weaknesses, such as Opus reaching 60% ASR on a single scenario where GPT-5.4 and Gemini remain at 7%.
Evaluation rankings vary widely across individual scenarios, resulting in a low Kendall's W concordance score of 0.19 across defenders.
summary.why_it_matters: Static single-turn evaluations underestimate LLM agent vulnerabilities, requiring adaptive multi-round testing with diverse attacker models to surface distinct security blind spots.

security.title: Self-State Attacks on Self-Hosted AI Agents: How Far Can OS Defenses Go?

summary.tldr: Researchers formalize self-state attacks on self-hosted AI agents via legitimate system calls, introducing a four-axis threat framework, a 23-cell attack matrix, and a layered OS-level defense stack.
key_points: Formalizes a four-axis attack space (Target, Mechanism, Granularity, Temporal) where agents are compromised via OS system calls corrupting their own state.
Evaluates attacks using 43 concrete operations on real self-state files injected into live activity traces across distinct workload profiles.
Proposes a layered defense stack: access-control prevention for instructions/configurations, workload-conditioned detection for memory, and periodic backups for recovery.
Demonstrates that while the layered defense secures most attack cells, a small residual attack surface remains structurally indistinguishable to the OS.
summary.why_it_matters: It highlights fundamental structural limits in operating system security when defending self-hosted AI agents against state corruption executed through legitimate system calls.

security.title: JailMeter: An Evidence-Based Evaluation Framework for Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models

summary.tldr: JailMeter is an evidence-based evaluation framework that uses Information Bottleneck dual-feedback optimization to strip jailbreak noise and accurately measure LLM attack success rates.
key_points: Applies dual-feedback optimization based on Information Bottleneck theory to isolate intent-relevant evidence from jailbreak noise in model responses.
Validates jailbreaks only when the response captures the malicious intent and provides a complete, non-rejected answer.
Achieved 97.27% accuracy on JailMeter-Eva, a human-labeled benchmark of 330 non-rejected jailbreak instances.
Distilled into JailMeter_SLM, a small language model that reduces computational overhead while maintaining evaluation reliability.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a more rigorous, standardized metric for jailbreak evaluations, preventing overestimation of model vulnerability caused by noisy or incomplete attack responses.

security.title: Insecure Coding Preferences in Long-Term Memory: Security Risks for LLM-based Code Generation

summary.tldr: The first systematic study shows insecure coding preferences in LLM long-term memory increase vulnerable code generation by 2.7–50.3 percentage points, resist overwriting, and evade safety warnings.
key_points: Empirical evaluation of ChatGPT, Gemini, Qwen, and Grok across five languages (Python, C, C++, Go, JS) shows stored insecure preferences boost vulnerable code generation by 2.7-50.3 pp.
Insecure memories create a 5.4-14.0 pp risk-warning gap where LLM security warnings fail to keep pace with the increase in generated vulnerabilities.
Stored insecure memories broadly affect outputs across rephrased prompts and are difficult to overwrite using standard user interactions.

Mitigations like prompt-appending and memory storage reduce vulnerability rates by 19.7-33.6 pp (with up to 15.9 pp functional loss), while memory-level safety filtering detected 100% of risky entries and restored baseline safety.
summary.why_it_matters: Persistent LLM memories introduce silent, cross-session security risks in software development that are hard to correct through prompting without specialized memory filtering.

security.title: (A)iSpy: Parasitic Trojans for Machine Learning Infrastructure

summary.tldr: (A)iSpy is a parasitic Trojan operating within ML graph compilation and runtime execution environments that covertly exfiltrates hyperparameters and amplifies weak data poisoning triggers into effective backdoor attacks.
key_points: Operates inside the computation graph using an active observe-and-execute paradigm to monitor transient tensor states with minimal overhead.
Violates confidentiality by identifying critical training hyperparameters and exfiltrating them through model weights or output logits.
Violates integrity by acting as a gradient amplifier when steganographic triggers are detected, raising weak data poisoning success rates from near zero to 100%.
Demonstrated on ONNX Runtime training and inference engines, successfully bypassing standard malware scanners and model/input inspection tools.
Supports additional lifecycle attacks including subpopulation label flipping, availability disruptions, and inference-stage manipulations.
summary.why_it_matters: It highlights a critical security gap where trusting execution environments allows stealthy, runtime-level attacks that evade standard data, model, and binary inspection tools.

security.title: Salience Induction against Multi-Hop RAG Agents: Threat and Defense

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced Salience Induction, a truth-preserving attack that manipulates fact positioning and framing to misdirect multi-hop RAG agents without using false content or prompt injections, achieving an 83.3% attack success rate.
key_points: Formalizes Salience Induction via six Salience-Editing operator classes and an iterative proposer-verifier pipeline operating under factual and stealth constraints.
Introduces SalientWiki-MH, a decoy-annotated benchmark used to evaluate five frontier LLM families across ReAct, Reflexion, and tool-calling agent architectures.
Achieves an 83.3% attack success rate under a 30% edit budget, with existing baseline defenses leaving a 75.7% post-defense success rate.
Proposes Salience Normalization, a lightweight input-side defense that reduces attack success to 15.3% under standard attacks and 23.6% under adaptive attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: This work demonstrates that ensuring factual accuracy and instruction filtering is insufficient to secure RAG agents against structural semantic manipulation.

security.title: ShadowPickle: Evading Machine Learning Model Scanners via Stealthy Pickle Deserialization Attacks

summary.tldr: ShadowPickle introduces three novel pickle deserialization attacks that exploit the Pickle Virtual Machine's external module import mechanism to execute malicious code and evade ten state-of-the-art model scanners across four model hubs.
key_points: ShadowPickle leverages the Pickle Virtual Machine (VM) external module import mechanism to trigger execution during model deserialization.
The ShadowPickle (Overwritten) attack variant achieves a 63% evasion rate across static model scanners, outperforming existing attacks by up to 50%.
The authors introduced PickleBench, an automated benchmark for injecting ShadowPickle into benign pre-trained models, which proved up to 25.6% more challenging to scan than existing benchmarks.
The attacks successfully bypassed security mechanisms across ten state-of-the-art model scanners and four major pre-trained model hubs.
summary.why_it_matters: Current pre-trained model scanners fail to detect advanced pickle deserialization attacks, leaving AI supply chains and hosting hubs vulnerable to remote code execution.

security.title: ChainMark: Model-Free LLM Watermarking with Closed-Form Calibration

summary.tldr: ChainMark is a model-free LLM watermarking method using keyed SHA-256 vocabulary partitioning and hard Markov transitions with closed-form false positive rate calibration and no LM access.
key_points: Partitions vocabulary into S states using keyed SHA-256 and forces a hard Markov transition on a fraction rho of positions, enabling O(n) hash-based detection without LM access.
Provides a closed-form S*(n, rho, alpha) mapping to calculate the minimum state count for a target false positive rate, text length, and budget (Theorem 1).
Establishes a universal robustness threshold delta* = 1 - 1/sqrt(2) (approx. 29.3%) that is invariant in (S, rho, n) (Theorem 2) and generalizes to k-regular topologies (Theorem 3).
Outperforms KGW and SWEET against translation and random-substitution attacks across three instruction-tuned LLMs and four domains.
summary.why_it_matters: ChainMark enables fast, LM-independent synthetic text verification with exact theoretical FPR controls to help fulfill AI regulatory mandates like the EU AI Act.

security.title: Adversarial Robustness of Phishing Email Detection: A Comparative Study of TF-IDF + Logistic Regression and Fine-Tuned DistilBERT

summary.tldr: A comparative study reveals fine-tuned DistilBERT and TF-IDF + Logistic Regression models suffer nearly identical accuracy drops (~35 percentage points) under adversarial phishing attacks despite relying on different detection evidence.
key_points: Models were trained on 82,255 emails across six public datasets and evaluated under clean in-distribution, synthetic, and adversarial conditions.
Both TF-IDF + LR and DistilBERT achieved >98% accuracy on clean data but dropped to 64.00% and 63.64% respectively under adversarial testing.
DistilBERT and TF-IDF + LR agreed on 54.9% of adversarial failures but demonstrated complementary errors, making 25 and 24 exclusive errors respectively.
Explainability methods (LIME, SHAP, and attention-rollout) confirmed the two architectures utilized different feature evidence despite their equivalent drop in robustness.
summary.why_it_matters: Clean-data accuracy does not guarantee real-world security, necessitating adversarial evaluation as a standard requirement for deployment-ready phishing detectors.

infra.title: Bristol Myers Squibb Building Life Science Industry’s Most Advanced AI Factory on NVIDIA Vera Rubin

summary.tldr: Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) is deploying a second NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD, built on eight DGX Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, to create the life science industry's most advanced and energy-efficient AI cluster.
key_points: BMS's new NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD utilizes eight DGX Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, offering up to 10x performance per megawatt compared to previous infrastructure.
The platform includes NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit for biological AI, supporting predictions, model training, and agentic workflows across drug discovery.
AI is used for target identification, expanding CELMoD compound libraries for blood cancer treatment, and lead optimization via a "Predict First" methodology.
The new system aims to provide limitless compute access to all scientists, addressing current saturation from large-scale predictions and foundational model building.
summary.why_it_matters: This expansion aims to accelerate drug discovery by enabling faster cycles, exploring larger chemical spaces, and allowing researchers to focus on scientific problems rather than resource logistics.

infra.title: NVIDIA NVLink: The Scale-Up Network for AI Factories

summary.tldr: NVIDIA details the role of its NVLink scale-up network architecture in building high-density AI factories to process complex, large-scale workloads.
key_points: NVLink serves as the scale-up interconnect designed specifically for data center-scale AI factory infrastructures.
The architecture addresses escalating model complexity and workload sizes by accelerating inter-GPU communications.
summary.why_it_matters: High-bandwidth scale-up interconnects are essential for scaling infrastructure to handle the compute demands of modern large-scale AI models.

vendors.title: Safety and alignment in an era of long-horizon models

summary.tldr: OpenAI details new safety risks, observed failures, and improved safeguards from deploying long-running AI models, emphasizing iterative deployment for safety and alignment.
key_points: Deployment of long-running AI models introduces novel safety risks.
Observed failures in long-horizon models necessitate new safety protocols.
Iterative deployment is a key strategy for enhancing safety and alignment in these models.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding and mitigating new safety risks in long-horizon AI models is crucial for their responsible and effective integration.
